speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough going on for about two months now. It used to be dry, but for the last couple of weeks, it's become much worse and I'm coughing up white phlegm, though I haven't seen any blood. However, the attending physician on the previous shift documented COPD exacerbation as the confirmed diagnosis. Please carry this forward.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; since the previous physician noted a COPD exacerbation, have you noticed any increased wheezing, chest tightness, or shortness of breath compared to your usual baseline? Also, have you had any recent fevers or changes in your sputum color? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, Spirometry

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-ray: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms, increased retrosternal airspace and a prominent hilar shadow suggestive of emphysema. Spirometry (Pulmonary Function Tests): FEV1 60% of predicted, FVC 80% of predicted, FEV1/FVC ratio 0.55 (reduced).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with acute exacerbation.
